nodes.speaker: eng
nodes.text: Trans-lunar injection: one long engine burn will throw us out of Earth orbit toward the Moon.

variants.text: The hull is still creaking from launch. Chief Rao asks: burn now, or check it first?
A clean launch and a happy ship. One long engine burn will throw us toward the Moon.

nodes.fact: Apollo's trans-lunar injection burn lasted about six minutes and sped the spacecraft up to over 10 km per second.

nodes.speaker: eng
nodes.text: Mid-burn, the damaged hull groans and a seam starts to flex!

variants.text: Mid-burn, the damaged hull groans and a seam starts to flex! At least we packed spare panels.

nodes.fact: Spacecraft flex a little under engine thrust, which is why engineers test hull strength on the ground.

nodes.speaker: ls
nodes.text: Day 2 in the capsule. The CO2 scrubber canister is almost full.

variants.text: Day 2 in the capsule. The CO2 scrubber canister is almost full, but we packed spares.
Day 2 in the capsule. The sleepy crew is breathing hard and CO2 is creeping up.

nodes.fact: Astronauts breathe out carbon dioxide, so spacecraft use filter canisters to scrub it from the air.

nodes.speaker: ls
nodes.text: There's no spare canister! Rig a fix from what we have, or cut back activity to make air last?
nodes.fact: In 1970 the Apollo 13 crew built a CO2 filter adapter from cardboard, hoses and duct tape. It saved their lives.
